patients.summary: Retired postal worker on Medicare and Medicaid who joins in 2017 with stage 5 CKD, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and hypertension, starts hemodialysis in late 2018 and then has anemia of CKD, treated pulmonary TB, an ED hypoglycemia, a pulmonary edema admission after missed dialysis and MSSA access bacteremia. Last seen May 2024; dialysis-related amyloidosis (2025) and normal pressure hydrocephalus (2026) reach the chart only as outside letters.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Washington phoned about moving his primary care to us. He lives in Williamsburg, has Medicare and MassHealth. Sees an outside kidney group already and wants a doctor closer to home who can coordinate. Takes insulin. Booked new patient visit 9/12, 75 min slot. Release form mailed so we can request his old office's records. Asked him to bring all his pill bottles and insulin pens.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65-year-old man new to the practice, transferring from an office he'd been at for years; wanted someone closer to home.

Kidneys: followed by an outside nephrology group for advanced CKD. Told at his last nephrology visit that he is at stage 5 and should plan access for dialysis. Not on dialysis. He has been putting off the vascular surgery consult - 'I'm not ready to think about the machine.' Makes urine, no swelling, appetite fair, no itching or nausea.
Diabetes: on insulin for many years. Glargine 24 units at bedtime, lispro by a sliding scale with meals. Checks sugars twice a day, mostly 140s-220s. Rare lows, none needing help.
BP: lisinopril 5 mg daily, nephrology manages dose.
Also on aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 40.

PSH: left carpal tunnel release, about 2013.
FH: father had a heart attack at 62. Mother with type 2 diabetes. Sister with high blood pressure.
SH: retired from the postal service on disability. Smoked about a pack a day for 40 years, quit around 2009. No alcohol. Lives in Williamsburg. Divorced; a daughter in the area.
Allergies: none to medications.

Exam: BP 144/86 on recheck, pleasant, no distress. Weight 86 kg, height 178 cm. Conjunctivae pink. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Both radial pulses full, no access in either arm. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. CKD stage 5, not on dialysis - nephrology owns this. Encouraged him to keep the vascular surgery appointment; better to have a fistula ready than start through a neck line. Labs today.
2. Type 2 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin - A1c today. Same doses for now.
3. Hypertension - a bit above goal today; nephrology to adjust.
4. Former heavy smoker - lung cancer screening at next visit.
5. Health maintenance - records request to his old office for colonoscopy and vaccines. Flu shot next month.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Washington, your bloodwork from Tuesday is in. A1c is 8.1 - a little higher than we'd like, but your sugars at home sound reasonable and I don't want to push the insulin while your kidneys are this weak, since lows become more likely. Kidney numbers are in the range your nephrologist has been watching, and potassium is okay. Cholesterol is well controlled on atorvastatin. Please send the results to your kidney doctor too, or I can fax them. See you in December.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from the patient's previous primary care office, 38 pages, received by fax. Includes problem list (type 2 diabetes on insulin, hypertension, chronic kidney disease), med list matching what he brought, and:
- Left carpal tunnel release April 2013, outpatient hand surgery.
- Screening colonoscopy June 2015: normal to the cecum, good prep, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Flu shots most years. No pneumococcal vaccine on file. Last tetanus over 10 years ago.
Abstracted into chart; paper copy to the scanning bin.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L deltoid, PCV13 R deltoid per PCP order. VIS given. No prior reactions. Afebrile. Waited 15 min, fine. Told him PPSV23 is due in a year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for 3-month check. Saw nephrology in November; they want him to see vascular surgery 'after the holidays.' Still has not booked. No new symptoms. Sugar log: fasting 130-190, one 74 before lunch after a long morning, felt shaky, ate.

BP as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Feet unchanged.

A/P
T2DM: A1c today. No change to insulin.
CKD 5: urged him again about the fistula consult. Will message nephrology that we're seeing him.
Lung cancer screening: shared decision discussion done - he qualifies (40 pk-yr, quit within 15 years). Wants it. LDCT ordered.
RTC 3 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose non-contrast CT of the chest, baseline screening exam. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Central airways patent. Mild coronary artery calcification. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT lung screening
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Baseline low-dose screening CT. No nodules. Lung-RADS 1. Next annual screen January 2019.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your lung screening CT was clear - no spots at all. We'll repeat it once a year while you qualify.

documents.title: Refill authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for lisinopril 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg and insulin lispro pens. Last visit 12/2017, next 3/20. Approved 90 days per standing refill protocol.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing ok. Some fatigue by afternoon, no worse than fall. Appetite fine. No itch, nausea, swelling. Vascular surgery consult still not scheduled - says the phone tree defeated him; we gave him the number again and the MA offered to sit with him while he called. He declined, will do it this week.

Exam: BP as charted. No JVD, lungs clear, no edema, no rub.

A/P: CKD 5 - nephrology following, labs today and copy to them. DM - A1c today, same insulin. Tdap today (none in 10+ years). RTC 4 months for wellness visit.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic eye exam, outside optometry office, 5/1/2018. Acuity 20/25 OD, 20/30 OS with correction. Lens: early nuclear changes, not visually significant. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye; no macular edema. Recall 1 year.

documents.title: Records to vascular surgery
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Vascular surgery office requested his recent labs and med list before his consult. Faxed last two visit notes, BMP and CBC with patient's permission.

orders.reason: one-time AAA screening, male former smoker 65-75

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.

Functional: independent in ADLs and IADLs. Drives short distances; daughter helps with longer trips. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine. Vision corrected, eye exam May - no retinopathy.
Mood: PHQ-2 = 0.
Cognition: recalls 3/3, clock normal.
Home safety reviewed, has smoke detectors.
Advance care planning: wants his daughter as health care proxy; form given to take home.

Medication review: glargine 24 at bedtime, lispro scale with meals, lisinopril 5, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40. Takes them as listed.

Kidneys: did see vascular surgery in June - vein mapping done, they want to schedule a left arm fistula 'in the fall.' Nephrology says dialysis likely within the year.

Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: intact, sensation normal, pulses good.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2015 normal, next 2025. PCV13 2017, PPSV23 due October. Tdap 2018. Shingles vaccine - will look into coverage. LDCT Jan 2018 negative, next Jan 2019. AAA screening ultrasound ordered.

Labs today: CMP, CBC, A1c, lipids.

reports.text: Limited abdominal aortic ultrasound for AAA screening. Abdominal aorta visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum diameter 2.0 cm, infrarenal. No aneurysm. Common iliac arteries normal caliber. Kidneys are small and echogenic bilaterally without hydronephrosis.

documents.title: AAA screening ultrasound
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Aorta 2.0 cm maximum. No AAA. Small echogenic kidneys, consistent with known chronic kidney disease.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
More tired, food tastes off for a few weeks. No vomiting, no confusion, no shortness of breath, no swelling. Nephrology saw him in August and told him to expect to start dialysis this fall. Fistula surgery was postponed once by the surgeon's office; now set for 'December.' He is anxious about it but resigned.

Exam: BP 142/84. Alert, a little tired-looking. No asterixis. Lungs clear, no rub, no edema.

A/P
CKD 5 approaching dialysis: BMP today, results to nephrology. Reviewed warning signs that need same-day care (breathlessness, confusion, vomiting, much less urine). Told him if dialysis has to start before the fistula is ready they will likely place a temporary neck catheter.
DM: stable, A1c from July 8.0. No change.
Flu and pneumococcal next month at nurse visit.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu and PPSV23 given, right and left deltoid. Pneumococcal series now complete per PCP. Tolerated well.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth with each meal

documents.title: Patient update: dialysis started
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know he started hemodialysis last Monday, 11/12. Labs at nephrology were worse and they didn't want to wait for the fistula. Had a tunneled catheter put in the right side of his neck on 11/9 at the hospital's IR suite. Goes Monday, Wednesday, Friday mornings, about 4 hours. Kidney doctor also started a phosphorus binder, sevelamer 800 mg with meals. Feels washed out after treatments but appetite better already. Fistula surgery still planned for December. Updated med list and problem list. Asked dialysis unit to fax monthly labs. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. ESRD now on HD MWF via R IJ tunneled catheter. Insulin needs may drop on dialysis - asked RN to remind him to call for any sugar under 80. Follow-up visit January.

procedures.procedure: Creation of upper limb arteriovenous fistula

documents.title: Vascular surgery operative note
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE NOTE - outside vascular surgery service. Date of surgery 12/11/2018.
Preoperative diagnosis: end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via right internal jugular tunneled catheter.
Procedure: left upper extremity arteriovenous fistula creation, radiocephalic not suitable on mapping; brachiocephalic fistula created.
Anesthesia: regional block with sedation. EBL minimal. Strong thrill at completion. No complications.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: hand exercises, check maturation at 6 weeks; continue dialysis via catheter until fistula usable; no BP cuffs or blood draws in the left arm.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months into HD (MWF). Tolerating it; tired on dialysis days, better on off days. Fistula made 12/11 in the left upper arm, healing, hand exercises. Still dialyzing through the right neck catheter. No fevers, catheter site clean per the unit. Sugars running a bit lower - fasting 110-160, no readings under 80. Dialysis unit is giving his hepatitis B series.

Exam (BP right arm only): as charted. Catheter dressing R chest clean and dry. L upper arm incision healed, good thrill and bruit. Lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
ESRD on HD - per nephrology. No BP or blood draws L arm, noted on chart banner.
DM - A1c today; no insulin change unless lows.
LDCT annual screen ordered.
RTC 3 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT compared with January 2018. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation. Right internal jugular dialysis catheter with tip at the cavoatrial junction. Mild coronary calcification, unchanged. No adenopathy or effusion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT lung screening
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Annual screen. Negative, Lung-RADS 1.

documents.title: Dialysis unit records
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Faxed from the outpatient dialysis unit.
- Admission labs 11/12/2018: hepatitis C antibody nonreactive, hepatitis B surface antigen nonreactive.
- Hepatitis B vaccine, dialysis dosing: 11/26, 12/24, 1/21, 3/18.
- Access: left brachiocephalic AVF cannulated from 3/4/2019 with two needles without problems; right IJ tunneled catheter removed in the unit 3/26/2019, site clean.
- March monthly labs (pre-treatment): K, CO2, BUN, Cr, Ca as listed; phosphorus 5.1, albumin 3.8.
- Schedule MWF first shift.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Catheter out last month, using the fistula now and 'glad to have nothing hanging off my neck.' Sugars steady. No lows below 80. No new complaints.

BP R arm as charted. L arm fistula with thrill. Lungs clear. Feet fine.

A/P: ESRD on HD via L AVF - stable. DM - A1c was 7.7 in January; recheck at July wellness visit. Dialysis unit labs reviewed. Refilled insulin pens and pen needles for 90 days.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual diabetic eye exam 5/14/2019. Dilated. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Mild nuclear sclerosis, stable. Return 12 months.

documents.title: Appointment question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I move my July appointment to a Tuesday or Thursday? Monday Wednesday Friday I'm at dialysis all morning and wiped out after. Thanks, Desmond

documents.title: Re: Appointment question
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Washington, you're now booked for Tuesday 7/23 at 9:00. We've added a note to your chart to schedule you on non-dialysis days.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.
Daily life: dialysis three mornings a week, rides from a neighbor or his daughter. Independent at home. No falls. PHQ-2 0. Memory concerns: none, 3-word recall intact.
Proxy form completed - daughter is his health care agent; scanned.
Meds reviewed and unchanged.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. L AVF thrill. No edema. Feet: no ulcers, monofilament intact.

Prevention: Shingrix dose 1 today; dose 2 in 2-6 months. Flu in October. Eye exam May normal. LDCT 2/2019 negative.
Labs: A1c, lipids, liver tests (statin), CBC.

documents.title: Prior authorization - insulin pens
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy says his plan now wants a PA for the glargine pens (formulary switch for the new plan year). Completed PA online with diagnosis and A1c history. Approved same day for 12 months. Pharmacy notified.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high-dose) R deltoid, Shingrix #2 R deltoid lower site. No left arm (fistula). After dose 1 he had a sore arm and felt tired for a day. Shingles series complete.

results.test: Reticulocytes/Erythrocytes in Blood by Automated count

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group - clinic note, visit 11/25/2019, copy to primary care.

Reason: tiredness and reduced stamina, worse over recent months.
He has now been on in-center hemodialysis for about one year, MWF via left brachiocephalic AVF. Reports tiring easily walking and with chores.

PMH: ESRD on HD, type 2 diabetes, hypertension.
PSH: L UE AV fistula; R IJ dialysis catheter (removed); L carpal tunnel release.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u qhs, insulin lispro sliding scale with meals, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI at 62; mother T2DM; sister HTN.
SH: ex-smoker 40 pk-yr, quit ~10 yrs. No alcohol. Retired postal worker on disability.

Exam: unremarkable.

Labs (pre-dialysis 11/25): Hgb 9.0 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, WBC 7.5, platelets 250. Smear: normocytic, normochromic red cells. Reticulocyte count low.

Assessment: anemia of chronic kidney disease, hypoproliferative.
Plan: start epoetin alfa 4,000 units IV with each dialysis; titrate to Hgb 10-11 by unit protocol. Iron indices with next monthly labs. Recheck 3-4 months.
